en.title: Modern Warfare 4 Beta Tests Divisive Matchmaking Alongside Open Systems
en.summary: The upcoming Modern Warfare 4 beta will feature a blend of matchmaking approaches, including the controversial skill-based system and last year's more open alternative. This move aims to gather player feedback on what makes for the most engaging online experience.
en.body:
The highly anticipated beta for **Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4**, set to kick off on August 21, 2026, will offer players a chance to test out its multiplayer matchmaking systems. In a significant decision that will undoubtedly spark debate within the community, the beta will feature both the newer, more complex matchmaking system introduced in **Black Ops 7 Season 5**, and the more randomized, open matchmaking that debuted with **Black Ops 7** last year.

This dual-system approach is Activision's latest attempt to navigate the choppy waters of player satisfaction regarding online lobbies. For years, the Call of Duty community has clamored for a matchmaking system that balances competitive integrity with enjoyable, less punishing gameplay. The older open matchmaking was a direct response to complaints about aggressive skill-based matchmaking (SBMM), which some players felt unfairly penalized them for performing well, leading to consistently difficult lobbies. Conversely, the newer system, which draws inspiration from the **Black Ops** titles, has been met with confusion and, for many, a less satisfying experience. Despite this sentiment, the Call of Duty team has stated that player retention has improved since its implementation, with fewer matches being quit overall.

## A Familiar Battleground for Matchmaking Debates

The inclusion of both systems in the **Modern Warfare 4** beta is a critical step for the developers. It allows them to directly gauge player preference and gather data on how each system impacts the overall gameplay experience. The newer system, as described by the development team, aims for "smarter team balancing, wide match variety, improvements that help keep matches full, and a better experience for mixed-level parties." However, many fans have pointed to the loss of persistent lobbies – where players could choose to stay in the same match after a game concluded – as a significant drawback of the newer system. This feature, which was largely absent in recent iterations but partially returned in **Black Ops 7**, allowed for more organic social interactions and a sense of community within matches. Its potential absence in **Modern Warfare 4** is a point of contention for a vocal segment of the player base.

## What This Means for Players

This beta period is more than just a preview of **Modern Warfare 4**'s content; it's a crucial feedback loop for Activision. The developers are keen to understand how these matchmaking adjustments align with the game's broader combat philosophy, which emphasizes making players "feel like they're really behind the gun." The success of this beta, in terms of player engagement and constructive feedback, could heavily influence the final matchmaking setup at launch. Players will have the opportunity to experience firsthand whether the new system, with its promise of better balancing, truly delivers a more enjoyable and varied experience, or if the more unpredictable nature of open matchmaking is what the community truly desires.

## The Road to Launch

The **Modern Warfare 4** beta begins August 21, 2026, with early access for those who have pre-ordered the game. The full release is scheduled for October 23, 2026. Players eager to dive in should keep an eye on official **Call of Duty** channels for specific access details and download instructions.

content_raw: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's beta will utilize a divisive new matchmaking system in addition to the open matchmaking introduced last year. Matchmaking is an extremely hot topic within the Call of Duty community, as it can dictate how much fun you might have playing online. Are you going to get steamrolled? Are you going to absolutely massacre the other team? A lot of that is in the hands of an algorithim pitting you against certain players. With Modern Warfare 4, the Call of Duty team has revealed its plans for what fans can expect in the beta this coming weekend . In a new thread, the Call of Duty team confirmed that the beta will feature the new matchmaking system introduced in Black Ops 7 Season 5, as well as the open matchmaking system that launched with Black Ops 7 last year . The open matchmaking is seen as being a bit more random, and as a result, more varied and dynamic. This was Call of Duty's answer to complaints about aggressive skill-based matchmaking, which some felt punished fans for performing well in games. The newer system, which is inspired by the matchmaking in the original two Black Ops games, has raised a lot of questions. Call of Duty noted in July that the new matchmaking system builds on what the studio has "learned, with smarter team balancing, wide match variety, improvements that help keep matches full, and a better experience for mixed-level parties." Many fans were initially confused on what exactly that meant, but many have ultimately found it to be less enjoyable than the open matchmaking. However, the Call of Duty team has revealed that players are actually quitting less matches since the implementation of the new strategy. In the open matchmaking from last fall, players were quitting more, getting less kills, and noting in surveys that they were having less fun. They went on to note that in the new matchmaking from this summer, some of their top players were facing tougher competition, but quitting less. As a result, MW4's upcoming beta will make use of both matchmaking systems so Infinity Ward can continue to mull over the data and make decisions on the full game. There has been no firm commitment on what kind of matchmaking the final game will use in October, though. We know some players like Open, but the issues were clear. For 80% of players in BO7 from launch to Season 04, Open vs. Standard saw: • 32.7% higher quit rates • 14.4% fewer kills per minute • 5.3% lower win rates • 59.2% more “Not Fun” ratings On Nuketown 24/7, quit rates… — Call of Duty (@CallofDuty) August 19, 2026 It's possible the data could change a bit, as MW4's beta could feature more players than Black Ops 7 in recent months. Modern Warfare is seen as the more popular Call of Duty subfranchise and a fresh new entry in the series is sure to attract new players during a time where there aren't a lot of games out. Only time will tell what happens, but if you have strong feelings one way or another, be sure to make your voice heard. I
